content.text:
I submitted index 11 (Co 0.29 / V 0.71) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 1.2e-6 A. All three merit measurements are used. I didn't spend any of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phases in these films are unconfirmed.

| Index | Co fraction | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | 0.54 | 3e-8 |
| 11 | 0.29 | 1.2e-6 |
| 2 | 0.196 | 8.6e-7 |

- **Where the peak sits:** photocurrent rises about 40-fold going from Co 0.54 to Co 0.29, then falls again at Co 0.196. With only three points, the best composition is most likely somewhere between Co 0.2 and Co 0.4. Index 11 lies between two known phases, CoV₃O₈ and CoV₂O₆.
- **Unmeasured candidates:** 5, 7 and 9 (Co 0.24–0.42) sit in that same window and might beat index 11. The Co-rich end (Co above 0.6) and the most V-rich end (Co below 0.16) are also untested.
- **What the models added:** the predicted band gaps for the Co–V phases are all below the 3.22 eV light (about 2.3 to 2.8 eV), so every phase should absorb it and the gaps didn't help rank candidates. The stability check found a V-rich Co vanadate close to stable (0.02 eV/atom above the hull). Together with the measured trend and the Gaussian-process model's top pick, that led me to choose index 2 as the last measurement.
